findings.text: Bounds query result carries an error indicator plus inclusive integer lower and upper limits for a parameter value.
Streaming input buffer holds a read-only start pointer, total byte extent, and a mutable read cursor; output buffer holds a writable start pointer, total extent, and mutable write cursor.
Both streaming cursors satisfy zero through size inclusive and are advanced by the library to record consumed input or produced output.
Sequence descriptor holds match offset, literal length, match length, and a small repeat-offset selector in range zero to three whose meaning shifts when literal length is zero.
An all-zero sequence denotes a block boundary marker, while a zero offset with zero match length denotes trailing literals of the stated literal length.
Compression parameter aggregate holds window size exponent, chain size exponent, hash size exponent, search effort exponent, minimum match length, target length, and a strategy selector.

Streaming compression and decompression contexts are aliases of the one-shot contexts, indicating a unified object; dictionary handles and context parameter storage are opaque forward-declared structures.
Header exposes a static-linking guard macro and maps the static API visibility macro to the shared visibility macro.

Encoder termination progresses from collecting input, to emitting at least one immediately decodable block while keeping history, to flushing remaining data and closing the frame so later input starts an independent frame.
Context reset supports three scopes: session only, parameters only, or both together.
Many compression and long-distance tuning values treat zero as select library default or automatic choice rather than a literal numeric setting.

Match length, hash size, hash rate, overlap, target block size and related tunables are clamped to documented minima and maxima, with effective minimum and maximum match sizes varying by strategy family.

Long-distance matching enlarges memory and effective window, changes default hash sizing relative to window, defaults minimum match around sixty-four and bucket exponent around three, and engages automatically for very large windows with higher strategies unless explicitly set.
Frame header flags default to including known content size and dictionary identifier while omitting the trailing checksum.

Worker count selects single-threaded blocking operation at zero versus asynchronous parallel compression at one or more; job size and overlap fraction only take effect with workers enabled and job size is floored to overlap or a half-megabyte minimum.
Overlap selector ranges zero to nine where zero is library default, one disables overlap, nine uses a full window, and intermediate steps halve load per decrement; default varies by strategy.

Streaming decoder refuses frames demanding a window beyond a default exponent limit to bound memory, overridable through the decompression maximum-window parameter; one-pass decoding without extra allocation is unaffected.
Experimental parameter identifiers and names are unstable, require static-linking access, and must not be used directly by stable callers.
Setting multithreading parameters without multithreaded build support is ineffective and reports an error; worker presence can be probed by setting at least one worker and checking the result.
Target compressed block size is only a convergence hint for latency-sensitive streaming, not a guarantee, and older implementations may regress if used.
Multithreaded flush and frame-end operations may block to emit as much output as possible, and an initial end request in streaming mode may delegate to blocking one-shot compression.

Compression parameter identifiers observed: search attempts 104, minimum match 105, target length 106, strategy 107, target compressed block size 130, long-distance enable 160, long-distance hash 161, minimum match 162, bucket size 163, hash rate 164, content-size flag 200, checksum flag 201, dictionary-id flag 202, worker count 400, job size 401, overlap 402.
Experimental compression slots use 500 then 10 then 1000 through 1017 with the 1003 slot repurposed; decompression maximum window uses 100 and experimental decompression slots use 1000 through 1005.
Reset directives are session only 1, parameters 2, both 3; end directives are continue 0, flush 1, end 2.

Search and match limits: window exponent 10 to 30 on 32-bit and 31 on 64-bit, hash exponent 6 to window-capped 30, chain exponent hash-minimum to 29 on 32-bit and 30 on 64-bit, search exponent 1 to window minus one, match length 3 to 7, overlap 0 to 9, default streaming window refusal exponent 27, minimum valid maximum block size 1024.

Framing sizes: maximum header 18 bytes, skippable header 8 bytes, with smaller format-dependent minima for header-size queries; long-distance ranges are hash 6 to hash-max, minimum match 4 to 4096, bucket 1 to 8, hash-rate 0 to window minus hash-min; target block range starts at 1340 up to maximum block and source-size hint spans 0 to maximum int.
